**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, the Exalted:**

[8–16] ﴿So do not obey the deniers﴾ ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9] ﴿And do not obey every habitual swearer, contemptible﴾ [al-Qalam: 10] ﴿A slanderer, going about with gossip﴾ [al-Qalam: 11] ﴿Preventer of good, transgressor, sinful﴾ [al-Qalam: 12] ﴿Brutal, and after that, ignoble﴾ [al-Qalam: 13] ﴿Because he has wealth and sons﴾ [al-Qalam: 14] ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Qalam: 15] ﴿We will brand him on the snout﴾ [al-Qalam: 16]

﴿So do not obey the deniers﴾: that is, those who deny the signs of God and the truth that came to them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: this is an incitement and a goading against their disobedience.

﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9]: that is, they wish you would incline toward their gods and abandon what you hold of the truth, so that they would conform to you. Ibn Jarir narrated this from Mujahid. Then he said: that is, if you were to soften toward them in your religion by responding to them and inclining toward their gods, they would soften toward you in your worship of your God. As His majesty, His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And had We not strengthened you, you would almost have inclined to them a little﴾ [al-Isra: 74] ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾ [al-Isra: 75].

It is derived from "al-duhn" (oil, lubricant): he likened softening in speech to the softening of oil.

﴿Every habitual swearer﴾ [al-Qalam: 10]: that is, one who swears often. Al-Zamakhshari said: it suffices as a deterrent for one who is accustomed to swearing. Similar is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle through your oaths﴾ [al-Baqarah: 224].

﴿Contemptible﴾ [al-Qalam: 10]: that is, of base opinion and discernment.

﴿A slanderer﴾ [al-Qalam: 11]: that is, one who defames and reviles. Ibn Jarir said: "al-hamz" originally means "al-ghamz" (pressing, pinching). So the backbiter is called "hammaz" because he attacks people's honor with what they dislike, and that is a pressing upon them.

﴿Going about with gossip﴾ [al-Qalam: 11]: that is, one who carries people's talk from one to another, to create discord among them.

﴿Preventer of good﴾ [al-Qalam: 12]: that is, stingy with wealth, withholding it. "Al-khayr" means wealth. Or it means one who averts people from Islam.

﴿Transgressor﴾ [al-Qalam: 12]: that is, against people, exceeding bounds in wronging them. ﴿Sinful﴾ [al-Qalam: 12]: one who commits many sins.

﴿Brutal﴾ [al-Qalam: 13]: that is, coarse, harsh, and of ill nature (da'iy). ﴿And after that, ignoble﴾ [al-Qalam: 13]: that is, one who is falsely attached to a lineage, not of them; or one of doubtful origin who is known for evil. Ibn Jarir said: the meaning of "ba'd" (after) in this place is the meaning of "ma'a" (with).

Al-Shihab said: the reference is to all the defects that came before it, not only the last one, and it is to indicate that what follows is greater in ugliness. So "ba'd" here is like "thumma" (then), which indicates a gradation in rank, as was mentioned in His saying: ﴿After that, [He is] a supporter﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4].

﴿Because he has wealth and sons﴾ [al-Qalam: 14]: Al-Zamakhshari said: it is connected to His saying "do not obey" [al-Qalam: 10]. That is: do not obey him with these defects, because he has wealth, that is, because of his affluence and his share of worldly life. It may also be connected to what follows it, in the sense: because he is wealthy and relies on his sons, he denied Our signs.

﴿When Our verses are recited to him﴾ [al-Qalam: 15]: that is, Our Book's verses are read to him. ﴿He says, "Tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Qalam: 15]: that is, this is something the ancients wrote, mocking him and denying that it comes from Allah.

His saying: ﴿We will brand him on the snout﴾ [al-Qalam: 16] is a promise from Him, exalted is He, of the utmost humiliation of him after the extremity of his arrogance, self-admiration, pride and insolence. The Arabs say: "I branded him with the brand of evil," meaning that he attached to him a disgrace that will never leave him. Jarir said:

*When I placed my brand on al-Farazdaq,
and on al-Bu'ayth I cut off the nose of al-Akhtal.*

Al-Zamakhshari said: the face is the most honorable place of the body, and the nose is the most honorable part of the face because it comes first on it. For this reason they made it the place of honor and zeal, derived from it the word "al-anafa" (pride), and said: "the nose is in the nose," "his nose was protected," and "so-and-so has a high nose." And for the humiliated they said: "his nose was cut off," and "his nose was rubbed in the dust." So he expressed the utmost humiliation and disgrace by branding on the snout, because a brand on the face is a blemish and degradation, so how much more so on the most honorable place of it? It is narrated that al-'Abbas branded his camels on their faces, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Honor the faces," so he branded them on their flanks. It was also said: the word "al-khurtum" is a demeaning of him and an insult, because the original meaning of "al-khurtum" belongs to the pig and the elephant. It was also said: "We will mark him on the Day of Resurrection with a disfiguring sign by which he will be distinguished from the rest of the disbelievers, just as he was hostile to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a hostility by which he was set apart from them." End of quote.

**Note:**

It was said that the verse refers to al-Akhnas ibn Shariq. Ibn Jarir said: his origin is from Thaqif, and his affiliation is among Banu Zuhrah; that is, because he joined them until he was one of them in the pre-Islamic period. For this reason he was called "zanim," for his attachment to the people while not being one of them. It was also said: it refers to al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, whose father claimed him eighteen years after his birth.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[17–18] "Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning, and did not make an exception (inshaa' Allah)."

"Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden": That is, We tried the polytheists of Makkah, testing them with this Wise Revelation, to see whether they would be thankful for His favour, so that they would live a good life, or whether they would persist in denying it, in which case their end would be nothing but like the end of the people of the garden in their trial that follows, and then their destruction.

It has also been said that its meaning is: We afflicted them with a calamity, namely drought and hunger, by the supplication of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "as We tried the people of the garden." They were a people from among the People of the Book, according to what is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, or people from Abyssinia according to the view of 'Ikrimah, meaning they were followers of a Book. This agrees with what precedes it. And it is not a necessary requirement for taking a lesson from the parable and its admonition to specify its people, were it not for the love of what is transmitted.

"When they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning": That is, that they would surely cut off its fruit early in the morning, in such a way that no poor person would know of it.

"And did not make an exception" [al-Qalam: 18]. Al-Mahayimi said: That is, they did not set aside any part of the right of the poor, and he restricted himself to this. Al-Razi and al-Qadi related it as a second opinion. The first is that its meaning is: they did not say, "if Allah wills." Ibn Jarir restricted himself to this. The first is more apparent. The istithna' (exception) here is in the sense of the physical removal (al-ikhraj al-hissi), and the sentence is coordinated (ma'tufah) with "they would surely harvest it" [layasrimunnaha], and is a clause sworn upon (muqsam 'alayha).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 68, verses 28–32:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28–32] ﴿The best of them in conduct said, "Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not glorify [Allah]?'"﴾ ﴿They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers."﴾ [Al-Qalam: 29] ﴿Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.﴾ [Al-Qalam: 30] ﴿They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we have been transgressors."﴾ [Al-Qalam: 31] ﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we are turning toward our Lord [in hope].﴾ [Al-Qalam: 32]

﴿The best of them﴾, i.e., the most just of them and the soundest in opinion, ﴿said, "Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not glorify [Allah]?'"﴾, i.e., (p-5901) remember Allah and repent to Him from the corruption of your intentions, and fear His retribution upon the criminals. The best of them had admonished them when they resolved upon their wicked resolution, but they disobeyed him, so he rebuked them.

﴿They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers."﴾ [Al-Qalam: 29], i.e., in neglecting to set aside the right of the needy and withholding the good from them from that garden. ﴿Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.﴾ [Al-Qalam: 30], i.e., some of them blamed others.

﴿They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we have been transgressors."﴾ [Al-Qalam: 31], i.e., exceeding the limits of Allah, exalted is He, in our neglect and our evil resolve. ﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it.﴾ [Al-Qalam: 32], i.e., through our repentance to Him, our regret over the error of our action, and our resolve never to return to the like of it.

﴿Indeed, we are turning toward our Lord [in hope].﴾ [Al-Qalam: 32], i.e., seeking pardon for what we neglected and compensation for what we missed.

(p-٥٩٠٥) Warning:

What we have related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, concerning the meaning of ﴿shin﴾ [al-Qalam: 42] is the apparent meaning, fitting the constant dreadful portrayal of that Day in verses like this one, and al-Zamakhshari confined himself to it. His expression is:

"Uncovering the shin, and revealing the *khidām* (the leg-covering or the lower part of the leg), is a figure for the severity of the matter and the difficulty of the calamity. Its origin is in panic and defeat, when veiled women lift up their shins while fleeing and reveal their *khidām* at that time." Hatim said:

*The man of war, if war bites him, it bites him back, and if war lifts its shin, it lifts its own shin.*

And Ibn al-Ruqayyat said:

*It distracts the old man from his sons and reveals,* ∗∗∗ *from the leg-coverings of the virgin noblewoman.*

It came indefinite (*nakira*) to indicate that it is an ambiguous matter in its severity, a strange thing outside what is familiar, like His words: ﴿On the Day when the caller calls to a terrible thing﴾ [al-Qamar: 6]. It is as if it were said: "On the Day when a terrible, awesome matter occurs."

(p-٥٩٠٥) Abu Saʿid al-Darir said: That is: On the Day when the origin of the matter is uncovered. The *sāq* (shin/shank) of a thing is its origin upon which its stability rests, like the trunk of a tree or the shin of a person. That is: on the Day of Resurrection the realities and origins of things will become manifest. So *sāq* in this sense means the origin of the matter, and it is a metaphor (*isti'āra*) derived from the trunk of a tree. In "al-Kashshaf" there is another figurative usage (*tajawwuz*), or it is an extension (*tarshīḥ*) of it.

Imam Ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy on him, said in "al-Fisal": What has been authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ concerning the Day of Resurrection is: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin, and they will fall down in prostration." This is as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in the Qur'an: ﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered and they are called to prostration﴾ [al-Qalam: 42]. It is only a report of the severity of the matter and the terror of the situation, just as the Arabs say, "The war has lifted its shin." Jarir said:

*Many a lofty-gazed man of the Ali Mazin, when the war lifted its shin, lifted himself up.*

It is strange that someone would deny these authentic reports, which have come with what the Qur'an has come with explicitly. But whoever's knowledge is narrow denies what he has no knowledge of. Allah has censured this, saying: ﴿Nay, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge﴾ [Yunus: 39]. End.

A parallel to this verse is His words: ﴿Why, when it reaches the throat?﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 83]. End.

So why do you say that this is not permissible? Then the Exalted emphasised their being frightened by the greatness of the Day of Resurrection, by making them fear what is with Him and within His power of subjugation, so He, glorified be He, said:

Then the Exalted emphasised their being frightened by the greatness of the Day of Resurrection, by making them fear what is with Him and within His power of subjugation, so He, glorified be He, said:

(p-٥٩٠٣) The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the deeper meaning of the verse) of His words, exalted is He:

[34–43] ﴿Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are Gardens of Bliss.﴾ ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35] ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 36] ﴿Or do you have a Book in which you study,﴾ [al-Qalam: 37] ﴿that you shall have therein whatever you choose?﴾ [al-Qalam: 38] ﴿Or do you have oaths binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that you shall have whatever you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 39] ﴿Ask them which of them will stand surety for that.﴾ [al-Qalam: 40] ﴿Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.﴾ [al-Qalam: 41] ﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered and they are called to prostration, but they will not be able.﴾ [al-Qalam: 42] ﴿Their eyes humbled, humiliation covering them, though they had been called to prostration while they were sound.﴾ [al-Qalam: 43]

﴿Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are Gardens of Bliss.﴾ ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35] That is: in honour, in the good reward, and in the praiseworthy final outcome.

﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 36] That is: by that which sound reason repudiates, for the two cannot be equal in this matter.

﴿Or do you have a Book in which you study,﴾ [al-Qalam: 37] ﴿that you shall have therein whatever you choose?﴾ [al-Qalam: 38] That is: of matters for yourselves, and whatever you desire for yourselves, as in His words:

﴿Or have We given them a Book from which they hold clear proof?﴾ [Fatir: 40] This is a rebuke and reproach for what they were saying of falsehood, (p-٥٩٠٤) and for the false wishes they were longing for. ﴿Or do you have oaths binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that you shall have whatever you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 39] That is: you decide according to your wishes and your claims.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is said, "So-and-so has an oath (*yamin*) upon me for such-and-such," when you have guaranteed it from him, and you have sworn to him to fulfil it. He means: Or have We taken on a guarantee from you and sworn to you with emphatic oaths, extremely strong in confirmation, ﴿that you shall have whatever you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 39], which is the answer to the oath, because the meaning of ﴿Or do you have oaths binding upon Us?﴾ [al-Qalam: 39] is "Or have We sworn to you?" As for *bāligha* ("binding"), as al-Shihab said, its meaning intended here is: "reaching its limit in confirmation." Its origin is *bāligha aqṣā mā yumkin* ("reaching the furthest that is possible"), which was shortened by omission, and this meaning became common. ﴿Ask them which of them will stand surety for that.﴾ [al-Qalam: 40] That is: for the judgement; ﴿surety (*za'īm*)﴾ [al-Qalam: 40] means one who guarantees it, claiming it and affirming it. ﴿Or do they have partners?﴾ [al-Qalam: 41] That is: people who share this claim with them and agree with them upon it.

﴿Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.﴾ [al-Qalam: 41] That is: in their claim.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that no one will grant them this, nor support them in it, just as they have no Book that speaks for it, nor covenant concerning it with Allah, nor surety who would stand by it. So this is an alert to the negation of everything they might cling to, whether by reason or by transmission.

﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered﴾ [al-Qalam: 42] Ibn ʿAbbas said: That is: from a severe, dreadful matter of the terror of the Day of Resurrection. Do you not hear the Arabs say, "The war has lifted its shin"? Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

﴿And they are called to prostration but they will not be able.﴾ [al-Qalam: 42] That is: because of the terrible torment that has encircled them and barred them. ﴿Their eyes humbled, humiliation covering them﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] That is: the humiliation of the disobedience of the past covers them.

﴿Though they had been called to prostration while they were sound﴾ [al-Qalam: 43] That is: there was no obstacle preventing them from it. What is meant by prostration is the worship of Allah alone, submitting one's face to Him, and acting upon what He commanded of righteous deeds.

(p-٥٩٠٥) Warning:

What we have related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, concerning the meaning of ﴿shin﴾ [al-Qalam: 42] is the apparent meaning, fitting the constant dreadful portrayal of that Day in verses like this one, and al-Zamakhshari confined himself to it. His expression is:

"Uncovering the shin, and revealing the *khidām* (the leg-covering or the lower part of the leg), is a figure for the severity of the matter and the difficulty of the calamity. Its origin is in panic and defeat, when veiled women lift up their shins while fleeing and reveal their *khidām* at that time." Hatim said:

*The man of war, if war bites him, it bites him back, and if war lifts its shin, it lifts its own shin.*

And Ibn al-Ruqayyat said:

*It distracts the old man from his sons and reveals,* ∗∗∗ *from the leg-coverings of the virgin noblewoman.*

It came indefinite (*nakira*) to indicate that it is an ambiguous matter in its severity, a strange thing outside what is familiar, like His words: ﴿On the Day when the caller calls to a terrible thing﴾ [al-Qamar: 6]. It is as if it were said: "On the Day when a terrible, awesome matter occurs."

(p-٥٩٠٥) Abu Saʿid al-Darir said: That is: On the Day when the origin of the matter is uncovered. The *sāq* (shin/shank) of a thing is its origin upon which its stability rests, like the trunk of a tree or the shin of a person. That is: on the Day of Resurrection the realities and origins of things will become manifest. So *sāq* in this sense means the origin of the matter, and it is a metaphor (*isti'āra*) derived from the trunk of a tree. In "al-Kashshaf" there is another figurative usage (*tajawwuz*), or it is an extension (*tarshīḥ*) of it.

Imam Ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy on him, said in "al-Fisal": What has been authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ concerning the Day of Resurrection is: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will uncover His shin, and they will fall down in prostration." This is as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in the Qur'an: ﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered and they are called to prostration﴾ [al-Qalam: 42]. It is only a report of the severity of the matter and the terror of the situation, just as the Arabs say, "The war has lifted its shin." Jarir said:

*Many a lofty-gazed man of the Ali Mazin, when the war lifted its shin, lifted himself up.*

It is strange that someone would deny these authentic reports, which have come with what the Qur'an has come with explicitly. But whoever's knowledge is narrow denies what he has no knowledge of. Allah has censured this, saying: ﴿Nay, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge﴾ [Yunus: 39]. End.

Now, Abu Muslim al-Isfahani went to the view that the verse is a worldly threat to the polytheists, not an otherworldly one. He said: It is not possible to carry it on the Day of Resurrection, because He, the Exalted, said in describing this Day: ﴿and they are called to prostration﴾ [al-Qalam: 42], and on the Day of Resurrection there is no worship or obligation in it. Rather, what is meant is either the last of a man's days in his worldly life, as in His words: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good news﴾ [al-Furqan: 22], and then he sees people being called to prayers (p-٥٩٠٦) when their times come, while he is unable to pray, because it is the time at which faith will not benefit a soul; or it is the state of old age, sickness, and incapacity. Before that they had been called to prostration while they were sound from what afflicts them now, either from the hardship that descends upon them from the terror of what they witness at death, or from incapacity and old age. A parallel to this verse is His words: ﴿Why, when it reaches the throat?﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 83]. End.

Al-Razi said: Know that there is no dispute that it is possible to carry the word upon what Abu Muslim said. As for his statement that it is not possible to carry it upon the Resurrection, on the grounds that the command to prostrate is present here and obligations cease on the Day of Resurrection, the answer is: That does not occur by way of obligation, but by way of rebuke and humiliation. So why do you say that this is not permissible? Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 68, verse 44:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse. We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know.﴾

﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse⦆ means: entrust their matter to Me, for I will suffice you against them. This is from eloquent metaphor (kinayah), as if He were saying: "It is enough of a retribution against him that you entrust his affair to Me and leave between Me and him, for I know what must be done to him and I am able to do it."

﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know⦆ means: We will outwit them by granting respite, continuing their health, and increasing their blessings, from where they do not know that it is a gradual drawing-on (istidraj) and a cause of their destruction. It is said: istadraja-hu ila kadha (he drew him on to such-and-such), meaning he brought him down to it step by step, degree by degree, until he entangled him in it.

(p-5907)

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[45] ﴿And I give them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm.﴾

﴿And I give them respite﴾ means: I grant them a reprieve and lengthen their terms for a measured period of time, so that the proof of Allah against them may be complete.

﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ means: My scheme against the people of disbelief is severe and powerful.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Health, provision, and the lengthening of life are a favor and bounty from Allah, which obligates them to gratitude and obedience, but they make it a means to disbelief by their own choice. So when they were led gradually by it toward destruction, he described the blessings as istidraj (gradual enticement). It was also said: How many are gradually enticed by kindness shown to them, how many are seduced by praise directed at them, and how many are deceived by being concealed from exposure. He called His kindness and His granting of power a "plan" just as He called it istidraj, because it takes the form of a plan, since it became a cause of their being plunged into ruin. He described it as "firm" because of the strength of the effect of His kindness in causing destruction.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[46–47] ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they can write it down?﴾ [al-Qalam: 47]

﴿Or do you ask them for a payment﴾ — i.e., for what you have brought them of sincere counsel, and what you have called them to of the truth.

﴿So that they are burdened with debt﴾ — i.e., they are weighed down by the heaviness of that payment: the paying of it burdens them, so they shun accepting your counsel and avoid entering into what you have called them to. Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[48–50] ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was suppressing [his grief].﴾ ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the open wasteland while he was blameworthy.﴾ [al-Qalam: 49] ﴿So his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.﴾ [al-Qalam: 50]

﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord﴾, which is their being given respite and the delay of your victory over them. That is, let their harm and their denial not turn you away from conveying what you were commanded, but proceed patiently in it. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, meaning Yunus, peace be upon him, ﴿when he called out﴾, that is, he called upon his Lord from within the belly of the fish, ﴿while he was suppressing [his grief]﴾, that is, filled with anger and distress. The meaning is: let there not be found in you what was found in him of impatience and slackness in conveying [the message), so that you are afflicted with his affliction. ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him﴾ [al-Qalam: 49], which is the acceptance of his repentance and His mercy, [and] his humble supplication and entreaty, ﴿he would have been cast onto the open wasteland while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Qalam: 49]. Al-Zamakhshari said: meaning that his condition was contrary to blame when he was cast onto the open wasteland, and had it not been for his repentance, his condition would have been one of blame. Al-'Ara' is the open expanse of the earth.

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾ [al-Qalam: 50], that is, by His mercy. Al-Qashani said: because of the soundness of his natural disposition, the survival of the light of his readiness, the absence of the firm establishment of the wrathful state, and his repentance from the lapses of the self, so the Exalted drew him near to Himself. ﴿And made him among the righteous﴾ [al-Qalam: 50], that is, for the station of prophethood and messengership.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[51–52] ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad."﴾ ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ [al-Qalam: 51–52]

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that they, from the intensity of their staring and their looking at you sidelong with eyes of enmity and hatred, would almost make your foot slip, or destroy you. This is from their saying: "He looked at me with a look that almost knocks me down, and almost devours me," meaning: if his look could cause me to fall or be devoured, he would do it. He said:

They exchange looks when they meet in a place, a look that makes the feet of footsteps slip.

Ibn ʿAbbas recited, when he passed by people who fixed their gaze upon him:

They looked at me with reddened eyes, a look like that of goats at the blades of the butcher.

God, exalted is He, made clear that this looking used to intensify from them while the Prophet (ﷺ) was reciting the Qur'an, and this is His words: ﴿when they hear the Reminder﴾, that is, the Qur'an, out of enmity toward its wisdom. ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad."﴾ That is, [they say he speaks] the raving that he utters in his madness, because they could not restrain themselves from envy of him and from repelling others away from him.

﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ [al-Qalam: 52] That is, it is an admonition, a wisdom, a reminder, and an alert for them, concerning what is in their minds and natural dispositions of monotheism. So how could one be called mad who has brought the like of this? And success is from God.
